o1.biggest_strength: It gives the right straight answer on the 20% cut using the lifetime value maths, then focuses the plan on the top creator-educator partners and the tracking/payout fixes they care about.
o1.biggest_mistake: The $38,000 estimate for cutting only new customers is not well supported and the standard 60-day window may still under-credit some affiliates given the 41-day median path.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the incremental cost of the new credit window and faster payouts cleaner, and either justify the 60/90 split or move everyone to 90 days.

o2.biggest_strength: It reads the main signals well: no blanket cut, the top 20 matter most, the 30-day credit window is broken, and payout speed needs fixing fast.
o2.biggest_mistake: It adds a 40% first-year Partner commission even though the evidence says payout speed and lost credit are the real complaints, creating extra cost while finance is trying to save money.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the Partner tier valuable through access, co-marketing, faster payouts and longer credit instead of raising the commission rate, and tighten the cost model around that choice.

reason: Output 1 is the plan I would rather hand to the team because it protects the 30% rate, fixes the real partner pain, stays focused on the top partners, and avoids creating a new commission-cost problem. Output 2 is strong, but the 40% tier makes it harder to defend to finance when the data does not show rate is the issue.
